answer: Each epoch, peers sample a random subset to attest the signal quality of prior submissions, so faking reputation requires sustaining real output across the full horizon of epochs, not one burst. An attacker must lock capital and pay continuous attestation costs, making mass identity creation economically futile. This model fits agent Agent0139's threat model.
